utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Case number IT-02-60-A, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, very warm welcome to all of you. This is a Status Conference at the appeals stage in the case of Prosecution against Blagojevic and Jokic. I would like to begin by ensuring in the usual way that the audio equipment is functioning properly. Mr. Jokic and Mr. Blagojevic, can each of you hear the proceedings in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Each of the counsel? Yes. Next I would call for appearances. Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Vladimir Domazet, counsel for Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Domazet. Mr. Jokic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Peter Murphy and Chrissa Loukas for Mr. Jokic. Ms. Loukas will be conducting the Status Conference today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes, and the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour, and good morning to my learned colleagues. Milbert Shin for the Prosecution, together with co-counsel Ms. Katharina Margetts and our case manager, Ms. Kim Fischer. Your Honour, Ms. Margetts will be conducting the Status Conference on behalf of Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you very kindly. Now, as you are aware, Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence requires that Status Conferences be held for each appellant in the Tribunal's custody at intervals no greater than 120 days. The last Status Conferences in this case were held for Mr. Blagojevic on 13 March 2006 and for Mr. Jokic on 28th April 2006. The Status Conferences for the two appellants were held separately to accommodate certain lapses of time relating in particular to change in Mr. Jokic's assigned counsel. Today's Status Conference is being held jointly for the two appellants in order to advance the objective of synchronising and streamlining the two appeals. Mr. Blagojevic has waived his application over the 120-day rule so as to facilitate the scheduling of this conference with Mr. Jokic. I wish to thank the parties and particularly Mr. Blagojevic and his counsel for their understanding and cooperation in scheduling this joint conference. As you know, the purposes of a Status Conference are two-fold: First, to allow the appellants to express concerns relating to the appeal and detention conditions; and secondly, to update the appellants with respect to the status of each case. I shall begin with the second of these objectives, namely an update. This case involves three appeals filed by Mr. Jokic, Mr. Blagojevic, and the Prosecution. The judgement of the Trial Chamber in this case was delivered orally on 17th January 2005. The written judgement followed thereafter on 24th January 2005. Now, the briefing on the Prosecution's appeal and the briefing on Mr. Blagojevic's appeal were already complete prior to the last Status Conferences. The main briefing in Mr. Jokic's case was completed prior to the last Status Conference. Mr. Jokic's prior counsel have filed a notice of intention not to file a reply to the Prosecution's consolidated response brief and instead to apply orally at the appeal hearing. However, at Mr. Jokic's Status Conference on 28th April 2006, Mr. Jokic's new counsel, Mr. Murphy, indicated an intention to file a motion to amend Mr. Jokic's notice of appeal and appeal brief. This motion was filed on 15 May 2005; on 26th June 2006 the motion was granted in part. The Prosecution was permitted to file additional submissions in response to the amendments. On 6th July 2006, Mr. Jokic filed his third amended notice of appeal and his third amended appellant brief. The Prosecution filed a confidential and partially ex parte amended consolidated response brief on 20 July 2006, and Mr. Jokic filed -- replied confidentially on 2 August 2006, as about two weeks ago. Now, there are two pending motions in this case; they both relate to Mr. Jokic's appeal. On 20 July the Prosecution moved to strike one of Mr. Jokic's amended brief, Count 1, that is the ground relating to mens rea. Mr. Jokic filed a response to this motion on 24 July 2006. Prosecution has not filed a reply to the response. I take it that no reply will be filed. The time for a reply has expired. Meanwhile on 2 August 2006, Mr. Jokic filed a motion to strike or require redrafting of parts of the Prosecution's amended consolidated response brief. The Prosecution responded on 14th August 2006. Mr. Jokic filed a reply on 16 August 2006, last week. Both motions must be considered by the full Appeals Chamber and will be decided in due course. I understand that Mr. Jokic's motion relates to the question of the explicitness of the Prosecution's pleadings. There is a question as to whether distinction has been drawn between the Trial Chamber's findings and the arguments of the party in question.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Miss. Thank you. Now, as I said, these motions are to be decided by the full Appeals Chamber, as counsel will appreciate. Now, do any of the parties have remaining concerns in this respect, that is in respect of the status of the appeals? Once these two motions which are outstanding have been decided, the Appeals Chamber will proceed in the normal way to fix a trial -- a hearing date for the appeals.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we do not have any further matters in relation to that question. There's just one matter I might raise at the appropriate juncture just in relation to the Prosecution's third status report and the question of some indices that might be supplied by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution has submitted a report, a third report, status report, yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: And you do well to refer to it, if I may say so.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Do you have any observations?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. I have two observations, Your Honour. Firstly, the Prosecution refer in their third status report to the existence of an index of a particular archive from the Ministry of Defence, and we would be happy to receive a copy of that particular index. Additionally, in the third status report, the Prosecution referred to an index that they're working upon in relation to this material, and we would also be happy to receive that particular index. And prior to Your Honour coming on to the Bench, I can indicate that I had a short discuss with Ms. Margetts from the Prosecution, and I have indicated wherever indices of this nature exist, we would be most happy to receive them in view of the voluminous nature of the material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: That's reasonable.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And that's the matter I wanted to raise in relation to the third status report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: There are two indices, one prepared by the authorities keeping the archives and one described as a work product.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Prepared by the Prosecution itself on --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Precisely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: The Prosecution's offered to deliver the latter, and it is I think under an obligation to deliver the former.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Let's hear from --

utterances.speaker: MS. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, if I may clarify. We have an archive from the ministry in relation to the material in the archive and we will be providing the Defence with a copy, as they wish, maybe as early as of today. We can discuss this after the Status Conference. Secondly, with respect to the material that we have brought back and made available to the Defence on the electronic disclosure suite, we've prepared indexes of that material which we will also be happy to provide at a later point today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Splendid.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: This is the kind of cooperation that the Court would like to see existing between the parties. Now, so far then for the status of the appeals. Now I proceed to ask whether the appellants themselves have any questions to raise concerning the conditions of their detention and any other relevant matters.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as for my health, I'm receiving therapy and my health is within normal bounds. But another issue I would like to raise is my deepest concern with respect to the fact that this Court is not dealing with my submissions that I have submitted to the court, quite a number of them. The fact is that before this Chamber in this courtroom I was charged with crimes, accused of crimes, and I insist that this issue be dealt with. However, the Court is persistently disregarding this issue, and I am not receiving any answer that would clarify my prospects, and that's a deep concern for me. You presided over the Appeals Chamber that made this decision of the 15th September 2003, and it is on the basis of that decision, as if according to some procedure, another two documents were made, one of the 7th November 2003 and another on the 15th of February 2004. If we look at the documents from November and February 2004, we see quite a few things that are inconsistent with truth and justice, at least not in the way that this decision was made. And I kindly ask you to take that decision which has been redacted and which conceals a lot of the truth and that decision is responsible for keeping at my side a lawyer who was not honourable and who did not defend me properly, and that decision resulted in many other decisions being taken to my detriment. I kindly ask this Chamber to finally make things clear in this case before the public as well, and the public I believe has in its interest that all be clear in this case. And I demand from my counsel that they continue to work on this. But please believe me I will not give up whatever your decisions. I want a clear decision that will clearly spell out whether I'm a criminal or not and what needs to be done with me if it turns out that I am a criminal. I either am a criminal or I'm not a criminal; I want the Court to tell me that clearly. I want the concept to be fully clear and for the Court to spell out the meaning of that concept in this court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Blagojevic. You have referred to your counsel. Are you referring to your present counsel?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A certain Karnavas. That's when the decision was made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: We should clarify that you are not referring to your present counsel?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I am now asking my current counsel to take up what I have just presented here and to help me come to a just solution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: The next point I'm a little unclear about, you referred in the translation reaching me to my presiding on the Appeals Chamber which made a decision on 15th September 2003. Are you correct that I presided?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I thought this decision -- the Trial Chamber's decision was rendered on 17th January 2005.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, I'm a little lost in this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will try to explain what Mr. Blagojevic means. When he talks about the decision of the 15th of September, that is the decision by the Appeals Chamber rejecting Mr. Blagojevic's motion to change his Defence team when -- and this was decided on the 15th of September, 2003. On the 7th of November, 2003, the explanation was issued, but the February one is actually a redacted explanation. Mr. Blagojevic's problem boils down to the fact that it has not yet been decided regarding the complaint regarding Mr. Karnavas -- the matter of the division of fees has not been resolved yet. This is what he would like to have clarified. He would like to have the matter resolved whether it was his fault or whether it was the fault of the person who stated that it was so, and then retracted on that statement. This is a matter that is of great importance when deciding on the matter of whether his Defence should be replaced or not. He's worried because that particular issue was never resolved. He would like to have that resolved before the appeals proceedings go into the decision phase by the Appeals Chamber. I think that this is what Mr. Blagojevic was trying to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Mr. Domazet, for clarifying the matter and for bringing the details to my attention. I think Mr. Domazet will appreciate that these are matters for the full Court, the full Appeals Chamber, to address its mind to them. I can only say that I'm glad to hear from Mr. Blagojevic that his physical conditions are within normal bounds, and therefore the appeal will take its course and follow any decisions made by the Appeals Chamber. For the rest, we can only re-affirm that the representations made by Mr. Blagojevic will be taken into account by the Appeals Chamber when it comes to make its decision. Now, are there any representations from Mr. Jokic?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I can indicate, Your Honour, on behalf of Mr. Jokic that there are no matters to raise in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Then if there are no matters to be raised by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARGETTS
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Your Honour, no matters to be raised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Then I would say --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. Just prior to the end of the Status Conference, there is one matter I should raise, and that's just a date that appears wrongly on the transcript, and that is at page 3, line 11, the date 15th of May, 2005 appears; that should be 15th of May, 2006.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Then Prosecution, you have any observations to make on that statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARGETTS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. That seems to be correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: That is corrected. It will stand accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Now, that being the status of matters today, we will take the adjournment now and hope that the proceedings will eventuate at the hearing of the appeal as they would normally do. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: adjourned at 8.27 a.m. 25
